sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia articles and publicly documented sources. Manali sits at 2050m in the Kullu Valley, Himachal Pradesh. Best season Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; Jul–Aug is monsoon with heavy rain and landslides on mountain roads. All records needs_review.

places.name: Hadimba Devi Temple
places.description: Pagoda-style wooden temple built in 1553 CE by Raja Bahadur Singh, set in a cedar forest at Dhungri. Dedicated to Hadimba (Hidimba), the consort of Bhima in the Mahabharata, worshipped as a local deity. The four-storey timber tower with carved panels is one of the finest examples of Himachali temple architecture. The forest setting — a grove of centuries-old deodars — is as notable as the temple itself. No entry fee; open most days, closed on certain puja days.
places.openingDays: Daily 08:00–18:00 (may be closed Tue and on specific puja dates)

places.name: Solang Valley
places.description: Open valley 14km north of Manali at 2480m, the main activity hub for adventure sports year-round. In summer (May–Oct): zorbing, paragliding, zip-lining, horse riding, and a ropeway/cable car to the upper slopes. In winter (Dec–Feb): skiing and snowboarding on snow-covered slopes. HRTC buses and shared taxis from Manali bus stand. Activity fees charged per activity by private operators; not a single-entry fee.

places.name: Rohtang Pass
places.description: High mountain pass at 3978m on the Manali–Leh Highway, 51km from Manali. Gateway to Lahaul–Spiti. Open May–Oct; closed by heavy snowfall Nov–Apr. Snow is visible at the pass even in June. The National Green Tribunal limits daily vehicle entries (around 1200 per day); permits must be booked online via the HP Tourism portal. Vehicles require a permit (fee per vehicle, not per person); the road to the top is steep and weather-dependent. Half-day or full-day excursion from Manali.
places.openingDays: Open May–Oct; permit required, daily quota applies

places.name: Vashisht Hot Springs
places.description: Natural sulphurous hot springs in Vashisht village, 3km from Manali's main market across the Beas River. Separate gender-segregated outdoor and indoor bathing tanks maintained by the community, fed by geothermal springs at high temperature. Free to use. Adjacent Vashisht Temple (dedicated to sage Vashisht, with Ram and Krishna shrines) is also free. The village retains a traditional Himachali character distinct from commercial Manali.

places.name: Old Manali
places.description: The original village settlement across the Manalsu Nala from modern Manali town, connected by a footbridge. The lower part has cafes, guesthouses, and an apple orchard atmosphere popular with backpackers and long-stay travellers. The upper part near Manu Temple retains its traditional stone-and-wood village character. Walking the lanes, trying local trout and Himachali cuisine, and exploring the orchard paths are the main draws. Free to visit.

places.name: Jogini Falls
places.description: Waterfall at approximately 2400m altitude, reached via a 3.5km trek from Vashisht village. The trail ascends through pine forest and apple orchards before opening to views of the Kullu valley. The falls drop in two main tiers through a rocky gorge. Round-trip takes 3–4 hours at a moderate pace. Largely unvisited compared to Hadimba and Solang; one of the better short treks near Manali for those who want to leave the tourist circuit.

places.name: Manu Temple
places.description: Small ancient Hindu temple in Old Manali dedicated to the sage Manu, the law-giver and progenitor of humanity in Hindu tradition. Claimed to be the only temple in India dedicated to Manu. Situated near the top of Old Manali village among traditional stone houses and apple orchards, a 15-minute walk uphill from the Manalsu bridge. The Pagoda-style wooden structure is architecturally similar to Hadimba Temple but far quieter. Free to visit.

places.name: Naggar Castle
places.description: 15th–16th century stone-and-wood castle at Naggar village, 22km south of Manali, built by Raja Sidh Singh of Kullu. Used by the British as a district rest house; restored and now operated as a heritage hotel by HP Tourism. A small museum inside displays local art and artefacts. The adjacent Nicholas Roerich Art Gallery holds paintings and memorabilia of the Russian artist and philosopher who lived and died at Naggar (1947). Views of the Beas valley from the castle terrace. Entry fee for non-hotel visitors.

places.name: Beas Kund Trek
places.description: Trek to the source of the Beas River at an alpine glacial lake (3540m), starting from Dhundi village 4km beyond Solang Valley. The well-marked trail passes through alpine meadows (bugyals) with views of Shitidhar, Hanuman Tibba, and Seven Sisters peaks. Possible as a strenuous day hike (16km round trip, 900m gain) or 2-day overnight. Route is generally open May–Oct. No permit required; guides available in Manali but trail is manageable with trekking experience.

places.name: Rahala Falls
places.description: Dramatic glacial waterfall at 2500m, visible from the Manali–Rohtang highway approximately 16km from Manali. Meltwater from the glaciers above Rohtang plunges in a wide cascade beside the road. A popular roadside stop en route to Rohtang Pass; vehicles stop for photographs. A short walk up the hillside allows a closer view. No entry fee; the area is open whenever the Rohtang road is passable (May–Oct).
places.openingDays: Open when Rohtang road is open (May–Oct)

places.name: Hampta Pass Trek
places.description: Classic 4-day Himalayan trek from Manali to the Chandra valley in Lahaul–Spiti via Hampta Pass (4270m). The route offers dramatic change of landscape: green forests and meadows on the Manali side give way to the stark moon-like terrain of Lahaul on the other. The trail passes through Jobra (base camp), Jwara meadows, and Shea Goru. Usually done guided; can be combined with a day visit to Chandratal Lake. Season: Jun–Sep. Porter and guide hire available in Manali.

places.name: Jana Waterfall
places.description: Cascade waterfall near Jana village, 11km from Manali on the right bank of the Beas (Naggar side). A 4km forest trail from the road winds through deodar and oak forest before reaching the falls. Much quieter than Rohtang-road waterfalls; a good alternative for those visiting Naggar. Best visited Apr–Oct; trail slippery after rain. Free to visit. Combined well with Naggar Castle as a day trip from Manali.

places.name: Manali Siddu and Dham Food Experience
places.description: Siddu is a steamed wheat bread stuffed with poppy seeds and walnuts — the traditional Himachali comfort food of Kullu valley. Best paired with ghee and dal. Dham (traditional feast) is served on occasions but local dhabas near Old Manali serve it daily.

places.name: Old Manali Café Scene
places.description: Old Manali village is packed with eclectic cafés serving Israeli breakfast, banana porridge, momos, and thukpa. Dragon and Drifters Inn are backpacker favourites. Great for people-watching, trip planning, and acclimatising before higher-altitude excursions.
